checked_claims.claim: raise_for_status catches HTTPError itself and ConnectionError only precedes a response
checked_claims.reason: raise_for_status raises HTTPError; separate response truthiness helper catches it, and transport errors can occur during response reads.

material_errors: raise_for_status raises HTTPError; separate response truthiness helper catches it, and transport errors can occur during response reads.
tasks.notes: Independent static inspection of pinned source; repository code was not executed. Scope is central claims, not exhaustive runtime verification.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: HTTPError and ConnectionError are sibling RequestException subclasses (src/requests/exceptions.py:55-60). Response.raise_for_status raises HTTPError with response=self for 4xx/5xx (models.py:1015-1026); it does not itself catch that exception. Adapter transport failures are mapped to ConnectionError or specialized subclasses (adapters.py:658-680). Callers can catch the common base or handle status failures separately from transport failures; transport failures are not restricted to initial connection establishment.

checked_claims.claim: list.remove is identity-only and cannot remove hooks registered via iterable
checked_claims.reason: list.remove uses equality; individual elements from iterable registration can be removed normally.

material_errors: list.remove uses equality; individual elements from iterable registration can be removed normally.
tasks.notes: Independent static inspection of pinned source; repository code was not executed. Scope is central claims, not exhaustive runtime verification.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: register_hook appends one callable or extends with callable elements from an iterable; it does not store the collection (src/requests/models.py:207-216). deregister_hook removes one matching element using list.remove and returns false if absent (218-227). Thus passing the original collection is not bulk deregistration, but its individual hooks can be removed. list.remove matches by equality, not exclusively identity; registration origin does not prevent removal.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: should_strip_auth first strips on hostname change. For the same host, it preserves auth on standard-port HTTP-to-HTTPS upgrades; the comment identifies backward compatibility as the reason (src/requests/sessions.py:127-143). It also preserves equivalent implicit/explicit default ports under the same scheme (145-154). Other scheme/port changes strip auth. This describes the code policy without asserting blanket RFC compliance.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: resolve_redirects first appends history, then consumes the current response (with raw-read fallback), checks redirect count, and closes it (src/requests/sessions.py:173-196). It rebuilds the next request and rewinds when _body_position is non-None and length/transfer headers are present (248-257); a failed-tell sentinel enters this path to raise UnrewindableBodyError. stream is passed to send, while intermediate redirect bodies are consumed regardless (265-272).

checked_claims.reason: Function only chooses a transmitted filename; it neither controls reading the file object nor guarantees receiver-side path safety.

material_errors: Function only chooses a transmitted filename; it neither controls reading the file object nor guarantees receiver-side path safety.
tasks.notes: Independent static inspection of pinned source; repository code was not executed. Scope is central claims, not exhaustive runtime verification.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: guess_filename reads obj.name, accepts a nonempty string not starting with < and not ending with >, and returns os.path.basename(name) (src/requests/utils.py:251-255). This avoids pseudo-filenames and strips local directory components for multipart metadata. It does not open or block streams, prove prevention of data exfiltration, or guarantee how a remote server handles filenames.
